description: The five canonical device scenarios used throughout the Meridian Pay documentation. Every value here is computed by the real server logic: device wire bits are translated through risk.FromWire, fused with attestation-derived bits, scored with risk.Score against the weights in this deployment's policy, mapped to a trust level by risk.Level, and turned into a decision by risk.Decision. Meridian Pay runs in ENFORCEMENT_MODE_STEP_UP.

scenarios.title: Genuine install on a healthy device
scenarios.story: A customer opens Meridian Pay on a stock, up-to-date phone. Play Integrity returns MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY for a registered build_hash.

scenarios.title: Rooted device, otherwise genuine app
scenarios.story: A power user runs the genuine app on a rooted phone. No tampering, no fraud overlay - just an elevated environment.
scenarios.note: Root alone is LOW_RISK and allowed; it is recorded for fleet analytics but does not gate a payment on its own.

scenarios.title: Repackaged build with patched SDK
scenarios.story: An attacker repackages the app. On-device self-integrity sees the binary no longer matches its build baseline; server-side attestation does not recognize the build.
scenarios.note: 60 + 70 = 130 lands exactly on the CRITICAL threshold. This is the only scenario that is denied outright. Detailed in trust/trust-decision.json and egress/webhook-body.json.

scenarios.title: Overlay + accessibility tapjacking during checkout
scenarios.story: A malicious accessibility service draws an overlay on top of the Meridian Pay confirm-payment screen to harvest the amount and PIN.
scenarios.note: 35 + 40 = 75 -> MEDIUM_RISK. The payment is held for a step-up re-authentication instead of completing silently.

scenarios.title: Remote-access scam in progress
scenarios.story: A victim is talked into a screen-sharing 'support' session while an accessibility service drives the app and a remote-access tool mirrors the screen.
scenarios.note: 30 + 40 + 45 = 115 -> HIGH_RISK. In STEP_UP mode this is a step-up challenge; in ENFORCEMENT_MODE_BLOCK the same level would be DECISION_DENY.
